## TL;DR

Implemented a passive, throttled RepoOS release notice for interactive CLI use, plus an `updates.check` setting that also gates the existing dashboard update banner. One shared `update-check` module caches GitHub lookups for 24 hours, reuses `fetchLatestRelease` and `upgradeInstruction` from `repoos upgrade`, and fails silently on network errors. Source checkouts and opted-out environments never nag.

## Work and rationale

Users only learned about new releases if they ran `repoos upgrade` or noticed the dashboard bell on their own. The task correction clarified that the dashboard banner and `GET /api/release/available` already existed (#1073 work); this task’s gap was the CLI stderr line and honoring a user-facing toggle on both surfaces.

I added `src/core/update-check.ts` as the single place for cache layout, eligibility rules, GitHub refresh, and CLI notice formatting. Semver comparison lives in `src/core/release-version.ts` so server, CLI, and tests share stable-vs-prerelease ordering without pulling in dependencies.

The CLI wires in at the end of `src/cli/index.ts`: after the command runs, `registerCliUpdateNoticeHook` optionally starts a background prefetch and registers a one-shot `exit` handler. Prefetch avoids adding latency to fast commands while still giving the ~1.5s GitHub request time to finish before the process exits on slower networks. The notice prints to stderr only when the install is standalone (not a source checkout), a newer version exists on the user’s channel, and the 24h notice throttle allows it.

Install-specific upgrade text comes straight from `upgradeInstruction` in `src/commands/upgrade.ts`, matching #1073’s server dialog. The cache file `~/.repoos/release-update-cache.json` stores `lastCheckedAt`, `latestVersion`, `url`, `dismissedVersion` (reserved for future cross-surface dismissal), and `lastNoticeAt` for CLI throttling.

On the server, `fetchAvailableRelease` in `src/server/routes/release.ts` now short-circuits when `updates.check` is false or the env opt-out is set, so the dashboard never fetches or shows an update when the user disabled checks. The Vue component consults `configStore.form["updates.check"]` so the banner hides immediately when the setting is off, without waiting for the next API round trip.

Configuration: `updates.check` defaults true, appears in `getConfigSchema()` with the usual Settings control, and is documented in `user-docs/configuration.md`, `user-docs/cli.md`, and `user-docs/environment-and-secrets.md` alongside `REPOOS_NO_UPDATE_CHECK`. Design notes are in `docs/update-check.md`, including the explicit “one anonymous GET, no telemetry” statement.

## Approaches tried

**Exit hook vs inline await:** Blocking every command with `await checkForRepoosUpdate()` would violate the “never slow a command” requirement. Prefetch at dispatch time plus a bounded synchronous wait in `emitCliUpdateNoticeOnExit` (using `Atomics.wait` in a tight loop) lets short commands exit quickly when the fetch is slow, while still allowing the notice when the prefetch completes within the timeout.

**Shared module vs duplicating upgrade logic:** Early sketches could have reimplemented install detection in the CLI hook. The correction and dependency on #1073 made reusing `releaseFromInstall` and `availableReleaseFromGithub` the right call—one comparison path for CLI, server cache refresh, and tests.

**Dashboard scope:** I did not add `GET /api/update-status` or a second banner; only the settings gate and server-side early return were needed per the task correction.

## Challenges and blockers

TTY and CI guards rely on `process.stdout.isTTY` / `process.stderr.isTTY` and standard CI env vars; vitest does not always emulate non-TTY, so the test suite focuses on env/config/`--json`/command skip list rather than stubbing TTY in every case.

The previous agent turn ended in a resume loop before handoff; the branch already contained WIP checkpoint commits with the full implementation, so this session verified tests locally and ran the scoped `repoos check` queue.

## Key learnings

Passive update checks fit best as “fire on exit, cache aggressively, share with existing release routes.” Throttling needs two clocks: `lastCheckedAt` for GitHub traffic and `lastNoticeAt` for stderr noise. Source installs must be excluded at comparison time, not only at notice print time, so dev trees ahead of latest tags never look “out of date.”
